name: Aloo Gobi
cuisine: North Indian (Punjabi home-style dry sabzi; also "aloo gobhi", "gobi aloo")

ingredients.name: Cauliflower (phool gobi), florets
ingredients.householdMeasure: about 1½ cups bite-size florets (¼ medium head)

ingredients.name: Potato (aloo)
ingredients.householdMeasure: 1 medium potato, cut into 2 cm cubes

ingredients.name: Sunflower oil (or mustard oil / groundnut oil)

equipment: Small kadai or heavy frying pan (7–8 inch) with a lid
Large bowl for washing the cauliflower, plus a colander
Measuring spoons (normal teaspoons are a fine stand-in)
Kitchen towel to dry the vegetables
Small bowl for the powdered spices

steps.title: Cut the cauliflower into florets
steps.text: Pull off the leaves, quarter the head and cut one quarter (about 150 g of florets) into 3–4 cm florets. Slice thick stems into thin rounds; they are edible.
steps.tip: Make the florets about the size of the potato cubes or slightly larger; cauliflower cooks faster than potato.
steps.visualCue: Even, bite-size florets of similar size, so they cook at the same speed.
steps.cameraCheck: The pile of florets on the board
steps.videoShot: The knife cutting a cauliflower quarter into small florets.
steps.watchOut: Mixing big and tiny florets, so the small ones turn to mush while the big ones stay raw; re-cut the big ones now.

steps.title: Soak the florets in warm salted water
steps.text: Put the florets in a bowl, cover with warm water and add ½ tsp salt (mostly drained away later). Leave 5 minutes while you prep.
steps.visualCue: Dirt settles at the bottom and any tiny insects float up or drift out of the florets.
steps.cameraCheck: The florets soaking in the bowl
steps.videoShot: Florets dropping into a bowl of steaming water.
steps.watchOut: Skipping the soak; Indian cauliflower can hide small green worms, and if you still see any, soak 5 minutes more and rinse.

steps.title: Peel and cube the potato
steps.text: Peel 1 medium potato (120 g), cut into 2 cm cubes and keep them in a bowl of water.
steps.visualCue: Even 2 cm cubes, pale and clean in the water.
steps.videoShot: The knife cubing a peeled potato.
steps.watchOut: Leaving cut potato out in the air, where it turns grey-brown; drop it into water straight away (the colour is harmless but looks poor).

steps.title: Chop the aromatics
steps.text: Finely chop the onion (40 g), tomato (50 g), ginger (1 tsp), garlic (1 clove) and green chilli.
steps.visualCue: Small, even pieces; the tomato in small dice.
steps.cameraCheck: Small heaps of onion, tomato, ginger-garlic and chilli on the board
steps.videoShot: Overhead shot of the chopped heaps.
steps.watchOut: Big uneven onion pieces, which stay crunchy in a short cook; chop smaller if they look bigger than a pea.

steps.title: Mix the powdered spices
steps.text: In a small bowl put ⅛ tsp turmeric, ½ tsp Kashmiri chilli powder and ¾ tsp coriander powder. Keep the garam masala, amchur and kasuri methi aside for the end.
steps.visualCue: A small mound of red, yellow and brown powders.
steps.videoShot: The three powders spooned into a bowl.
steps.watchOut: Adding the powders to dry hot oil one by one, where they burn in seconds; having them pre-mixed lets you add them in one go.

steps.title: Drain and dry the vegetables
steps.text: Drain the cauliflower, rinse once, and drain the potato. Spread both on a kitchen towel and pat dry.
steps.visualCue: No water dripping; surfaces look only slightly damp.
steps.cameraCheck: The drained florets and cubes on a towel
steps.videoShot: Hands patting the vegetables dry in a towel.
steps.watchOut: Wet vegetables, which steam instead of browning and make the oil spit; pat them again if the towel soaks through.

steps.title: Heat the oil and crackle the cumin
steps.text: Put the kadai on medium heat, add 2 tsp (10 ml) oil, then ½ tsp cumin seeds.
steps.tip: If using mustard oil, heat it until it just smokes, then let it cool for 30 seconds before adding the cumin.
steps.visualCue: The cumin sizzles, darkens one shade and smells toasty within about 20 seconds.
steps.videoShot: Cumin seeds sizzling in shimmering oil.
steps.watchOut: Cumin that turns black at once or smells bitter, a sign the oil is too hot; take the pan off the heat for a few seconds, and if the seeds are burnt, wipe the pan and start again.

steps.title: Fry the onion
steps.text: Add the chopped onion and stir on medium heat.
steps.visualCue: The onion turns soft and translucent with light golden edges, and smells sweet.
steps.videoShot: The spatula stirring onions that are turning golden.
steps.watchOut: Dark brown or burnt edges, which taste bitter; lower the heat and add 1 tbsp water if they darken before turning soft.

steps.title: Add the ginger, garlic and green chilli
steps.visualCue: The raw smell of garlic goes, replaced by a fragrant, sharp aroma.
steps.cameraCheck: The kadai with onion, ginger, garlic and chilli
steps.watchOut: Garlic that turns brown (it goes bitter) or a raw smell that stays; stir constantly and move on at the first fragrant whiff.

steps.title: Add the potato cubes
steps.text: Add the potato, stir to coat in oil, and fry uncovered on medium heat, stirring every 30 seconds.
steps.tip: Potato goes in first because it takes longer to cook than cauliflower; most sources agree on this.
steps.visualCue: The potato edges look slightly translucent and a few corners turn golden.
steps.cameraCheck: The potato cubes in the kadai
steps.videoShot: Potatoes tossing in the onion mixture.
steps.watchOut: Potato stuck to the base in a crust; scrape it with the spatula and sprinkle 1 tbsp water.

steps.title: Add the cauliflower
steps.text: Add the florets and stir gently.
steps.visualCue: Florets are coated in oil and a few spots turn light golden.
steps.cameraCheck: The potato and cauliflower together in the kadai
steps.videoShot: Florets going into the kadai and being folded in.
steps.watchOut: Crowding the pan so the vegetables steam in a pile; if the pan is small, keep them in as thin a layer as you can.

steps.title: Add the spice powders and salt
steps.text: Turn the heat to low. Add the spice bowl and ⅓ tsp salt. Stir gently for 30 seconds.
steps.visualCue: Every piece looks evenly yellow-orange, and the spices smell roasted, not burnt.
steps.videoShot: Spices sprinkled over and the vegetables turning yellow.
steps.watchOut: A sharp acrid smell and dark specks, meaning the spices are burning; add 1 tbsp water at once and lower the heat.

steps.title: Add the tomato
steps.text: Add the chopped tomato and stir.
steps.visualCue: The tomato starts to soften and release a little juice.
steps.cameraCheck: The tomato on top of the vegetables
steps.videoShot: Tomato dice tumbling into the kadai.
steps.watchOut: Adding tomato puree or too much tomato, which makes the sabzi wet; stay with the 50 g of fresh chopped tomato.

steps.title: Sprinkle water and cover
steps.text: Sprinkle 2 tbsp water around the edges, cover and cook on low heat.
steps.tip: Stir by lifting from underneath, not by mashing.
steps.visualCue: Steam builds under the lid, and the tomato melts into a thick coating on the vegetables.
steps.cameraCheck: The covered kadai, then the vegetables when you lift the lid
steps.videoShot: The lid lifting off to release steam.
steps.watchOut: Too much water, which gives a curry, or none, which burns the base; keep to 3 tbsp in total and add 1 tbsp only if the base sticks.

steps.title: Check doneness
steps.text: Press a potato cube and a cauliflower stem piece with the spatula.
steps.visualCue: The potato breaks easily; the cauliflower is tender but holds its shape with a slight bite.
steps.cameraCheck: A potato cube and a floret on the spatula, pressed
steps.videoShot: A knife sliding into a potato cube.
steps.watchOut: Hard potato at the centre (cover and cook 2–3 min more) or collapsing cauliflower (switch to uncovered at once).

steps.title: Dry it out and brown lightly
steps.text: Remove the lid, turn the heat to medium and cook uncovered, stirring gently every minute.
steps.visualCue: No liquid left at the bottom; the vegetables look dry and glossy with a few golden-brown patches.
steps.cameraCheck: The dry sabzi in the kadai
steps.videoShot: The vegetables sizzling with no liquid in the pan.
steps.watchOut: Stirring hard, which mashes the cauliflower to crumbs, or leaving liquid in the pan, which gives a soggy result; stir gently and cook until the bottom is dry.

steps.title: Add the finishing spices
steps.text: Switch off the heat. Sprinkle ¼ tsp garam masala, ¼ tsp amchur and ½ tsp crushed kasuri methi (rub it between your palms), and the chopped coriander leaves. Toss gently.
steps.visualCue: Flecks of green and brown over the sabzi; it smells warm and slightly tangy.
steps.cameraCheck: The finished aloo gobi with coriander on top
steps.videoShot: Kasuri methi being crushed between palms over the pan.
steps.watchOut: Adding garam masala on a very hot pan, where it turns bitter; switch the heat off first.

steps.title: Taste and serve
steps.text: Taste a piece and adjust with a pinch of salt or amchur. Cover for 2 minutes, then serve in a bowl.
steps.visualCue: Golden-yellow, dry, chunky sabzi with soft potato and just-tender cauliflower.
steps.videoShot: Aloo gobi spooned into a bowl next to a hot roti.
steps.watchOut: Salt added too late tasting raw on the surface; mix well after adding, and if too salty, add a few more cooked potato cubes or a squeeze of lemon.

reasons: a vegetable-only dish with just 2 tsp oil, no frying, no cream and 8–9 g fibre per bowl; cauliflower adds vitamin C and K and the spices add flavour without calories. Points come off because protein is low (about 7 g), potato makes it starch-heavy and the salt gives about 42% of the sodium limit. Restaurant and dhaba versions often deep-fry the vegetables first or use 1 tbsp or more of oil or ghee, plus more salt.

researchRating.basis: aloo gobi is one of North India's most-cooked everyday sabzis, and every major Indian recipe site carries it. Swasthi's Recipes shows a near-perfect score (4.99 from 590 votes in the latest snapshot; 4.98 from 630 in an older one); Veg Recipes of India's version has many pages of reader comments (comment page 5 was seen); Tarla Dalal, Hebbar's, My Ginger Garlic Kitchen, SBS and Feasting at Home also carry it. Small deduction because it is seen as simple, and some find it bland or mushy when overcooked.

storage: Refrigerate in an airtight box within 2 hours of cooking. Keeps 2 days in the fridge (the cauliflower smell strengthens after that). Freezing is not recommended; the potato turns grainy and the cauliflower watery. Reheat with 1 tsp water, covered, in the microwave for 1–1½ min, or in a pan on low heat for 3–4 min, stirring gently, until steaming hot.
leftoverRemix: Aloo gobi paratha (or toastie). Mash 1 cup leftover aloo gobi with a fork, add 1 tbsp chopped onion and a pinch of chaat masala, stuff into rolled wheat dough and cook on a tawa with ½ tsp oil per side. Or sandwich it with a cheese slice and toast it in a sandwich maker.
burnOff: about 3.8 km of running (265 ÷ 70 kcal/km, 70 kg adult), or about 5.3 km of brisk walking (about 65 min at 5 km/h, about 50 kcal/km) (est.). This is for the sabzi alone; 2 phulkas add about 2–2.5 km of running.

navratri.reason: drop onion and garlic, use sendha namak, and omit garam masala and any packaged spice mix; potato is commonly eaten, but cauliflower is not on many vrat lists, so an aloo-only version is the safe one (common rule set assumed)

ekadashi.reason: drop onion and garlic and skip hing; vegetables are generally allowed, but practice varies by family

jain.reason: see Jain variant; drop potato, onion, garlic and fresh ginger (roots) and use sonth

ramadan.reason: vegetarian, so no halal-meat issue; filling and fibre-rich for sehri with roti or dal, though protein is only about 7 g (est.) and the salt is moderate (about 2 g)

jain.reason: drop potato, onion, garlic and fresh ginger (all roots); use sonth (dry ginger powder) and a non-root vegetable such as capsicum or raw banana (see Jain variant). Some Jain households also avoid cauliflower; Not found as a single rule

vegan.reason: vegetables, spices and sunflower oil only; no dairy, ghee, honey or egg

sattvik.reason: skip the onion (40 g) and garlic (3 g) and add a little more tomato (see Sattvik variant)

glutenFree.reason: no wheat, rava, maida or hing in this recipe (do not add hing: most hing sold in India is compounded with wheat flour)

dairyFree.reason: no dairy in the recipe (do not swap in ghee)
